# Caddy — custom-to-root-context

Proxy at /app/, app at root /. handle_path strips the prefix on the way in, and two header_down regexes put it back into Location and every Set-Cookie on the way out, since Caddy has no ProxyPassReverse and no proxy_cookie_path. Requests outside the prefix get an explicit 404: an unmatched request in Caddy is otherwise an empty 200.

Proxy URL on `http://localhost:9090`: `/app/`

## Configuration

See [docker-compose.yml](./docker-compose.yml) for service definitions.

Caddy site block (`caddy/templates/strip-prefix.caddyfile`), mounted as
`/etc/caddy/vaadin.caddyfile`:

```caddyfile
# Proxy at /app/, app at root /. handle_path strips the prefix on the way in;
# two header_down regexes put it back on the way out.
#
# The two response headers are the only things the backend says about its own
# location, and Caddy repairs them with the same tool for both: there is no
# ProxyPassReverse and no proxy_cookie_path, but header_down applies a regex to
# every value of a header, so one rule rescopes JSESSIONID and csrfToken alike.
:80 {
	import common

	# NGINX answers the bare prefix with a redirect to /app/; this does the same.
	redir /app /app/ 308

	handle_path /app/* {
		reverse_proxy vaadin:8080 {
			header_down Location ^(https?://[^/]+)?/(.*)$ $1/app/$2
			# Anchored on the end of the value rather than on what follows the
			# path: Tomcat writes `Path=/; HttpOnly`, and a regex that expects
			# another path segment after the slash matches nothing at all —
			# which from the outside looks exactly like a rule that was not
			# needed.
			header_down Set-Cookie ^(.*;\s*[Pp]ath=)/(;.*)?$ $1/app$2
		}
	}

	# A request no handler matches gets an empty 200 from Caddy, not a 404.
	# NGINX has nothing outside its location, so neither does this.
	handle {
		respond 404
	}
}
```

The global options and the `common` snippet this file imports (the
access log and the compression allowlist) come from the shared
[Caddyfile](../../Caddyfile), mounted read-only over the image's own
`/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`. It imports this file, so the two only load as a pair.
